column2: agreed merge:hotelero, but hotelera is also a feminine noun in its own right (a hotel company, 'la hotelera'); check whether a second real word hides behind the merge
agreed merge:pagado; the reviewers' questions note it could equally be the participle of pagar (merge:pagar); check the target
agreed drop as a car-model name, but cabrio is an ordinary Spanish noun for a convertible car, and cabrío (macho cabrío) is a real adjective; check for a common-word reading
agreed drop as a transit brand, but metrobús is a common noun in several countries (a bus rapid transit line); possible merge:metrobús
agreed drop as a brand, but kleenex is widely used generically in Spanish for a paper tissue ('un kleenex'); check whether that counts as an ordinary word
agreed drop as a Catalan hospital name; Hospital Clínic de Barcelona may count as a nationally famous public institution under the institutions ruling
agreed drop as mostly a name, but jora is a real Andean Spanish word (chicha de jora, fermented maize); check whether the common word is a minority reading
